parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
State the effect of a catalyst on a reaction.
Explain how a catalyst causes this effect.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the meaning of the term heterogeneous as applied to catalysts.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Some bond energies are given.

| bond | bond energy/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{S=O}$ (in $\text{SO}_2$) | 534 |
| $\text{O=O}$ | 496 |

Use the data, and the enthalpy change for the conversion of sulfur dioxide into sulfur trioxide, to calculate a value for the $\text{S=O}$ bond energy in $\text{SO}_3$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The Contact process is usually carried out at a temperature of about $400^{\circ}\text{C}$ and a pressure just above atmospheric pressure. Using a higher or lower temperature and pressure would affect both the rate of production of sulfur trioxide and the yield of sulfur trioxide.

A reaction pathway diagram for both the catalysed and uncatalysed reactions between $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

The letters A-E represent energy changes.

Complete the table by stating which letter, A-E, represents the energy change described.

| energy change | letter |
| :--- | :--- |
| the energy change for the production of $\text{SO}_3$ |  |
| the activation energy for the production of $\text{SO}_3$ in the absence of a catalyst |  |
| the activation energy for the first step in the decomposition of $\text{SO}_3$ in the presence of a catalyst |  |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
The equation for this stage of the Contact Process is shown.

$$2\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H = -196\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
parts.text: State and explain the effect of increasing temperature on the rate of production of $\text{SO}_3$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain the effect of increasing temperature on the yield of $\text{SO}_3$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The $\text{SO}_3$ produced is converted to sulfuric acid in two stages. In the first stage the $\text{SO}_3$ is reacted with concentrated sulfuric acid to produce oleum, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$.
The oleum is then reacted with water to form sulfuric acid.

Suggest an equation for the reaction of oleum, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$, with water to form sulfuric acid.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{SO}_2$ reacts with water to form sulfurous acid.
Sulfurous acid is a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid, while sulfuric acid is a strong Brønsted-Lowry acid.
parts.text:
Complete the 'dot-and-cross' diagram to show the bonding in a molecule of $\text{SO}_2$. Show outer electrons only.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: State the meaning of the term strong Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text: Write an equation to show the acid-base behaviour of sulfuric acid with water. Include state symbols.
